children.translated_text: || <s>Avayavinirākaraṇam</s> (Refutation of the Composite Whole) ||
|| Homage to <s>Lokanātha</s> (Lord of the World)
Such excellence of practice has not been achieved, nor such learning acquired,
yet if I now, out of restlessness, endeavor to produce even a small portion of meaning—
let the wise examine all that has been stated, considering everything;
usually delight the minds of parents. ||
for indeed, the playful efforts of a child

children.text: यो विरुद्धधर्माध्यासवान् नासावेकः । यथा घटादिरर्थः । विरुद्धधर्मा
ध्यासवांश्च स्थूलो नीलादिरर्थ इति व्यापकविरुद्धोपलब्धिः । इह
children.translated_text: the gross blue and similar object—this is the apprehension of what contradicts the pervader (<s>vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhi</s>). Here,
the per-

children.text: मानः स्थूलो नीलादिरर्थो धर्मी । स चानुभवावसितोऽसति बाधके प्रत्यक्ष
children.translated_text: ceived gross blue and similar object is the subject (<s>dharmin</s>). And being ascertained through experience, in the absence of a defeater, established by perception,
it removes the defect of the locus being unestablished for the reason.
That which possesses the superimposition of contradictory properties is not one—just like a pot and similar objects. And possessing the superimposition of contradictory properties,

children.text: ननु भवद्भिरसन्नेवावयवी प्रतिज्न्ँआयते, स कथं प्रत्यक्षसिद्धः ? नावय
विनमिह धर्मिणं प्रतिपन्नाः स्मः, किं तु प्रतिभासमानं स्थूलनीलादिक
children.translated_text: whole as the subject here, but rather the appearing gross blue and such

children.text: मर्थम् । न तर्हि विरुद्धधर्मसंसर्गादवयविन एकत्वं प्रतिषिद्धं
children.translated_text: object. [Objection:] Then the oneness of the composite whole would not be refuted through the conjunction of contradictory properties
Objection: But you assert the composite whole (<s>avayavin</s>) to be simply non-existent; how then can it be established by perception? We do not accept the composite

children.text: चेत् ? स किं प्रतिभासमानात् स्थूलनीलादेरन्योऽनन्यो वा ? न तावदन्यः,
children.translated_text: is it different from or non-different from the appearing gross blue etc.? It is certainly not different,
since it is accepted as being perceived. And nothing else appears apart from the appearing gross blue object.
If non-different, then when the oneness of that is rejected, how can the oneness of the composite
whole remain unrejected?
If so, then what is the composite whole according to you? [Reply:] If [you say] it is a single entity inhering (<s>samaveta</s>) in many parts,

children.text: ननु च प्रतिभासमानश्चेदर्थो नावयविरूपो धर्मी, किं तर्हि रूपमस्या

children.translated_text: undifferentiated and established—
will there be? It is said: The appearing gross blue form—

children.text: प्रत्यक्षसिद्धं रूपम् अवयवित्वानभ्युपगमेऽप्यवशिष्यते । न चैवं मन्तव्यम् ।
children.translated_text: a nature established by perception—remains even without accepting composite-wholeness. And one should not think thus:

children.text: न परमाणुसंचयवादिनां स्थूलाकारः कश्चिदर्थोऽस्ति, यः प्रसिद्धो धर्मी
children.translated_text: 'For proponents of the aggregation of atoms (<s>paramāṇusaṃcayavādin</s>), there is no gross object that could be an established subject.'
For even without accepting the composite whole, a gross object constituted of many partless entities being accepted—
by whom has it been prohibited?
But if the appearing object is the subject and not in the form of a composite whole, then what nature of it—

children.text: स्यान्मतम्, निरवयवाः परमाणवः कथं प्रत्यक्षे स्थूलेनाकारेणाव
भासेरन्, स्थूलसूक्ष्मयोर्विरोधादिति ? तदपि न युक्तम्, परमाणव एव हि
children.translated_text: given the contradiction between gross and subtle? That too is not valid, for atoms themselves,
produced with mutual exclusion of the spatial locations of other forms, appearing together with one another,
appear as having extension in space. And extension in space is grossness.
One might think: How could partless atoms appear in perception with a gross form,

children.text: यत् तूक्तम्, स्थूलसूक्ष्मयोर्विरोध इति, तत् किं पररूपदेशपरिहारवती

children.translated_text: spatial locations of other forms, or the appearance of mutually associated entities in a single cognition,
constitute what is contradictory?
That is what is being asserted.
As for what was said—that there is a contradiction between gross and subtle—does the production of partless entities with mutual exclusion of the
then how is the gross form contradictory? Therefore, in the case of many partless entities

children.text: बहुष्वेकस्मिन् विज्न्ँआने प्रतिभासमानेषु भवन् प्रतिभासकालभावी प्रतिभास
children.translated_text: appearing in a single cognition, being present at the time of appearance, the gross form is a property of appearance—

children.text: धर्मः स्थूलाकारो न तु वास्तवः, प्रत्येकमभावात् । प्रतिभासात् प्राग् उर्ध्वं
children.translated_text: not a real property, since it is absent in each individually. Before or after appearance,

children.text: वा न तर्हि स्थूल इति चेत्--न, तदापि प्रतिभासयोग्यतासं
children.translated_text: would it not be gross then? [Reply:] No, because even then the fitness for appearing

children.text: भवात् । यदैव हि संचिता भवेयुः, तदैव प्रतिभासयोग्याः परमाणवः । यदा
children.translated_text: is present. For whenever they are assembled, at that very time the atoms are fit for appearing. When
they are fit for appearing, then they are gross.
If this is not contradictory,

children.text: भासितव्यम् । अन्तरानवभासे परस्परविविक्ता एव नावभासिताः स्युः ।
children.translated_text: appearing—[arguing that] without the appearance of intervals, they would not appear as mutually distinct.

children.text: विविक्तानवभासे चाणुमात्रकं पिण्डो भवेत् । न चान्तरमवभासमानमुत्प
children.translated_text: And without the appearance of distinctness, the aggregate would be merely atom-sized. And we do not per-

children.text: श्यामः । तदयं निरन्तर एक एव स्थूलो न
children.translated_text: ceive any interval appearing. Therefore this, being without intervals, is one single gross entity and not
constituted of many partless entities,

children.text: मर्हति, अपि त्वेकः स्थूलात्मक एवेति । सोऽप्येवं वाच्यः । किं विजातीय
children.translated_text: but rather is one single gross entity. To that one too, the following should be said: Is the interval a heterogeneous
atom between atoms, or is it contact with empty space? In that case, contact with empty
space, being unreal, is not within the range of sense perception; and where [perception] arises from the capacity of the object, only the object's
appearance is reasonable. But how could what is heterogeneous and graspable by another sense faculty appear in the cognition of a different sense,

children.text: अवभासेत, अविषयत्वात् ? तत्र केनान्तरेणावभासितव्यमिति न विद्मः ।
children.translated_text: since it is not an object of that sense? Therefore, we do not know by what interval [the atoms] must be made to appear.
But one who says that when many partless entities are appearing, there must necessarily also be an interval

children.text: यत् पुनरुच्यते, अन्तरालानवभासे विविक्ता नावभासेरन्निति, तत्रापि
किमेषामन्तरं विवेकः पररूपशून्यता वेति चिन्त्यम् । निरूपयन्तस्तु पररूप
children.translated_text: one should consider whether their interval is distinctness or the absence of the form of another. Upon examination, the absence of the form of another

children.text: शून्यतामेव विवेकं वस्तूनां पश्यामः । पररूपशून्याश्चेमे भासमानाः कथं
children.translated_text: is indeed what we see as the distinctness of things. And these, appearing as devoid of the form of another, how would they
not appear as distinct?
As for what is further said—that without the appearance of intervals, they would not appear as distinct—in that case too,

children.text: ननु च न प्रत्येकं परमाणूनां स्थूलाकारः, ततः समुदितानामेष्टव्यः ।
यथा च नीलपरमाणूनां प्रत्येकमसंभवन् पीताकारो बहुष्वपि न दृश्यते,
children.translated_text: And just as the yellow form, which is impossible in individual blue atoms, is not seen even in many blue atoms,

children.text: तथा प्रत्येकमसंभवन् स्थूलाकारः कथं बहुषु स्यादिति ?
children.translated_text: so too, how could the gross form, which is impossible in each individually, exist in many?
Objection: But there is no gross form in individual atoms; therefore it must be sought in them collectively.

children.text: उक्तमत्र, अविरुद्धो निरवयवाणां स्थूलाकार इति । नीलविरुद्धस्तु
पीताकारः । ततः पीतविरुद्धं नीलाकारं विभ्राणेषु बहुष्वपि कथं पीताकारो
children.translated_text: Therefore, how could the yellow form arise even in many atoms that bear the blue form, which contradicts yellow?

children.text: भवेत् ? नैवं निरवयवत्वविरुद्धः स्थूलाकारः, यथोक्तन्यायात् । तदेवं
children.translated_text: The gross form does not contradict partlessness in the same way, for the reason already stated. Thus,
it is established that the gross object, established by perception, is the subject here.
[Reply:] It has been stated here that the gross form is not contradictory for partless entities. But the yellow form contradicts blue.
having examined whether the reason exists or does not exist in the subject—
there, with a hand

children.text: दावेकस्मिन् कम्पमाने स्थूलोऽर्थः सकम्पनिष्कम्पे रूपे युगपत् प्रतिपद्यमानः
children.translated_text: and so on, when one part is trembling, the gross object, simultaneously assuming both trembling and non-trembling forms,

children.text: कथं विरुद्धधर्मसंसर्गवान् न स्यात् ? सकम्पनिष्कम्पयोर्हि रूपयोः परस्परा
children.translated_text: how could it not possess the conjunction of contradictory properties? For between the trembling and non-trembling forms, the mutual
contradiction is caused by invariable concomitance with the absence of each other. For it is only between existence and non-existence that there is a mutual

children.text: परिहारात्मको विरोधः । वस्तुनोस्तु तदभावाव्यभिचारेणैव । इह च सकम्प
children.translated_text: exclusionary contradiction. But for real things, it is only through invariable concomitance with the absence of that other. And here, the trembling

children.text: निष्कम्पे रूपे गृह्णत् प्रत्यक्षमेव सामर्थ्यात् परस्पराभावं साधयति ।
children.translated_text: and non-trembling forms—perception itself, grasping them, establishes from its own capacity their mutual absence.
It is bare non-apprehension alone that occasions the practical usage.
With the subject thus established,

children.text: रूपमभ्युपेयम् । अवयव एव हि तदा क्रियावान् दृश्यते । न चेदं
children.translated_text: form. For it is only the part that is then seen as possessing action. And one should not

children.text: मन्तव्यम्, अवयवे क्रियावति तदाधेयेनावयविनापि क्रियावता भवितव्यम्,
children.translated_text: think thus: 'When the part possesses action, the composite whole resting upon it must also possess action,

children.text: यथा रथे चलति तदारुढोऽपि चलतीति । अवयवावयविकर्मणोर्भिन्ननिमित्त
children.translated_text: just as when a chariot moves, one mounted upon it also moves.' For the actions of the part and the composite whole have different causes,
and the causes are not simultaneous.
One might say this: When one part such as a hand is trembling, the composite whole does not have the trembling

children.text: यदा हि आत्मनः पाणिकम्पनेच्छा भवति, ततः प्रयत्नः, तदा
प्रयत्नवदात्मपाणिसंयोगात् पाणौ क्रिया । यदा तु शरीरकम्पनार्थः प्रयत्नविशेष
children.translated_text: from the conjunction of the effortful self with the hand, action arises in the hand. But when a specific effort for the purpose of moving the body

children.text: आत्मनो जायते, तदा तत्प्रयत्नवदात्मशरीरसंयोगात् शरीरे कर्मेति निमित्त
children.translated_text: arises in the self, then from the conjunction of the effortful self with the body, action arises in the body—thus the difference in causes.
Therefore,
when one of two actions having different causes has arisen, how could the other, whose production depends on a different cause,

children.text: तदभावे तदपरोऽपि तथैव जायेत ? रथतदारुढकर्मणोस्तु सत्यपि निमित्त
children.translated_text: arise in the same way in the absence of that cause? But for the actions of a chariot and its rider, even though the causes
are different, they coexist due to the simultaneity of the causes.
For when the self (<s>ātman</s>) has a desire to move the hand, there arises effort, and then

children.text: तथा हि नोदनं रथकर्मणीऽसमवायिकारणम्, तदारुढकर्मणस्तु नोद्य
संयोगः । तयोश्च सहभावात् कर्मणी अपि यौगपद्येन जायेते । तदेतत्
children.translated_text: is the non-inherent cause. And since these two are simultaneous, the two actions also arise simultaneously. Now, all this
having been considered,
by the venerable <s>Dharmottara</s>,
the following was stated: 'And here the part does not possess action.'

children.text: अवयवेषु हि क्रियावस्तु विभागो जायते, क्रियाया विभागारम्भं प्रति निरपेक्ष
children.translated_text: For in the parts, what arises as action is actually separation (<s>vibhāga</s>), since action is an independent
cause for the production of separation. And thereby, when the conjunction that is the non-inherent cause
ceases, the composite whole—which is a
substance—would also cease.
For the impelling is the non-inherent cause of the chariot's action, while for the rider's action, the conjunction with what is impelled
the disciples of <s>Kaṇāda</s>:
from impelling or striking,
the action that arises—
a particular type of action is observed to produce a separation that opposes the conjunction that produces the substance. Other action, however, produces only separation

children.text: मात्रमारभते, न तु यथोक्तविशेषम् । अन्यस्मिन् पद्मसंकोचविकाशादिके
children.translated_text: of the ordinary kind, not the specific type mentioned. In other cases such as the contraction and expansion of a lotus,
since the cessation of the conjunction of parts is not observed. Likewise, action born of effort also
does not have the capacity to remove the conjunction. Therefore, there is no cessation of the substance.
Here, the following is said by

children.text: अयमत्र समाधिः । इहावयविनि क्रियावति नियमेनावयवैरपि क्रिया

children.translated_text: action. Otherwise, there would be separation from the spatial locations associated with the parts, and conjunction with spatial locations not associated with the parts,

children.text: सृष्टैश्च संयोगोऽवयविनः क्रियावतः स्यात् । अवयवास्तु क्रियाविरहिणः
children.translated_text: for the composite whole possessing action. But the parts, devoid of action,
would not move away from the previously occupied spatial locations. Nor would they come into contact
with the locations occupied by the composite whole.
Here is the resolution of this. When the composite whole possesses action, the parts must also necessarily possess
conjunction and separation of the effect are not accepted as causes of the conjunction and separation of the cause.
For it is the conjunction and separation of the cause that produce the conjunction and separation of the effect.
And the conjunction and separation of the parts cannot be said to arise from the conjunction and separation of the composite whole, since the

children.text: न च विपर्ययः, सिद्धान्तहानिप्रसङ्गात् । तेनावयवावयविनां पृथग्देश

children.translated_text: locations,
and since the relation of supporter and supported would be lost, even <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) would not hold. Therefore,
when the composite whole possesses action, the parts possess action—this must be accepted even unwillingly
by the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>.
This must be

children.text: पेयम् । यथा चावयविक्रियायामवयवाः क्रियावन्तः, तथा अवयवेष्वपि
children.translated_text: accepted. And just as the parts possess action when the composite whole has action, so too when the parts

children.text: क्रियावत्सु तदवयवैः क्रियावद्भिर्भाव्यमिति । अनया दिशा द्व्यणुके क्रिया
children.translated_text: possess action, their sub-parts must also possess action. By this reasoning, when a dyad (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>) possesses action,
the two atoms that constitute it must be understood as possessing action.
And the reverse is not the case, because it would lead to the abandonment of the established doctrine. Therefore, since the parts and composite whole have separate spatial

children.text: नस्तु निष्क्रियाः । परमाणुक्रियायां तदारब्धमपि द्व्यणुकद्रव्यं क्रियावत्
children.translated_text: are motionless. But when atoms possess action, even the dyad substance produced by them would possess action—
this would follow, since the action of all parts necessarily entails the action of the effect.
Therefore, atoms associated with moving parts are moving, and atoms associated with motionless parts

children.text: एकस्य परमाणोः क्रिया न परस्येति चेत् ? सक्रियनिष्क्रियौ तर्हि

children.translated_text: The two atoms, being separated from each other, would lose the conjunction that initiates substance. And then

children.text: द्रव्यनाशः । एवं च द्व्यणुकद्रव्यस्य क्रियावत्त्वे त्र्यणुकेऽपि क्रिया स्यादित्यनेन
children.translated_text: destruction of the substance [would follow]. And thus, if the dyad substance possesses motion, motion would also apply to the triad, and by this
progression, what is observed as stationary would become moving — that would be the part. Therefore, the motionless atoms connected with motionless parts,
being separated from the moving [atoms] connected with moving parts,
would lose the substance-initiating conjunction. For the atom, being partless, occupies an atomic-measure space

children.text: परिहारेण विरुद्धौ न वस्तुनी । वस्तुनोस्तु परस्पराभावाव्यभिचारेण
children.translated_text: contradicted by mutual exclusion, not [two] real things. But for real things, contradiction is through invariable concomitance with mutual absence.

children.text: विरोधः । तेन यदेव वस्तु वस्त्वन्तरप्रच्युतिमत्, तदेव तेन विरुद्धम् ।
children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever real thing possesses departure from another real thing, that alone is contradicted by it.
By this, what someone says is refuted — namely, 'Just as a single entity producing effects in this and that location is not

children.text: लम्भो हि वस्तुनो वस्त्वन्तराभावाव्यभिचारं साधयति । एककार्यनिर्वर्तन
children.translated_text: apprehension establishes the invariable concomitance of a thing with the absence of another thing. But when a form possessing the capacity to produce

children.text: शक्तिमति च रूपे गृह्यमाणे कार्यान्तरनिर्वर्त्तनशक्तिरपि परिच्छिद्यत इति
children.translated_text: one effect is apprehended, the capacity to produce another effect is also ascertained —

children.text: कथं तदभावः ? एकदेशसंबद्धं तु रूपं देशान्तरसंसर्गिरूपपरिहारेणोपलभ्य
children.translated_text: how then can there be the absence of that? But a form connected with one location, being apprehended to the exclusion of a form connected with another location,
[is such that]
it is invariably concomitant with the absence of that [other form], and hence contradicted by it. Just as, for two extremely similar things
perceived simultaneously,
even when there is a difference of appearance not discerned from a distance, [their] difference of location
alone, ascertained by perception as the ground,
is relied upon as the contradiction by which difference is established.
And the capacity to produce one effect is not invariably concomitant with the absence of the capacity for another effect. For non-

children.text: यस्त्वाह--यथैकं चक्षुर्विज्न्ँआनं भिन्नेषु चक्षुरादिषु वर्तते तदधीनोत्पाद

children.translated_text: because its arising depends on them, so too another [entity]
that lacks cessation in different locations will not be differentiated' — he too, when the contradiction based on difference of location
is being established, by imputing contradiction based on difference of cause to the real thing,

children.text: न नैपुण्यमात्मनो निवेदयति । न हि विज्न्ँआनस्य देशोऽस्ति कश्चित्,
children.translated_text: does not display his own cleverness. For consciousness has no location whatsoever,
being immaterial.
As for him who says — 'Just as a single visual cognition (<s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>) exists in the distinct [causes such as] the eye and so forth,

children.text: स्यादेतत् । यथा देशभेदनिमित्तो विरोधः, तथा कारणभेदनिमित्तोऽपि
स्यात् । को हि वस्तुतो विशेषः कारणभेदाद् देशभेदस्येति ?
children.translated_text: contradiction based on difference of cause. For what real distinction is there between difference of cause and difference of location?
It might be [objected]: Just as there is contradiction based on difference of location, so too there might be
That is present in the case of difference of location,

children.text: संनिधीयते, न कारणभेदे । देशभेदवती हि रूपेऽन्योन्य
children.translated_text: not in the case of difference of cause. For forms apprehended
to the mutual exclusion [of each other], possessing difference of location, are invariably concomitant with mutual absence, but not
those possessing [merely] difference of cause.
This has been addressed: the contradiction of real things is based on invariable concomitance with mutual absence.

children.text: तदेवं कम्परागावरणभावाभावकृते देशभेदनिबन्धने च चतुर्थे विरुद्ध
धर्मसंसर्गेऽवयविविषये व्यवस्थापिते पक्षधर्मत्वं सिद्धं हेतोः । अधुना व्याप्ति
children.translated_text: obscuration by vibration, color, and so forth — with respect to the composite (<s>avayavin</s>) as the subject, the property of belonging to the thesis is established for the reason. Now, the pervasion
of this [reason] with its probandum must be demonstrated.
Thus, having established the fourth [type of] contact with contradictory properties (<s>viruddhadharmasaṃsarga</s>) — based on difference of location caused by the presence and absence of

because it is impossible without a cause, and because no other ground is seen. Therefore, the conventional usage of non-difference, even when occurring in the case of contact with contradictory properties,
would abandon the pervading
ground of being a cause. Hence, by non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>),
what is excluded from that
is pervaded by the absence of contradictory properties. And the contradictory of that is contact with contradictory
properties. Therefore, this is of the form of apprehension of what contradicts the pervader (<s>vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhi</s>).
Here, the conventional usage of non-difference of real things is observed to be grounded merely in the absence of contact with contradictory properties,
find no scope.

Thus, when the triple characterization (<s>trairūpya</s>) of this [reason] has been established, the faults of being unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), and inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>)
Thus, by me, after the many thorns of objections
produced by the dull-witted have been uprooted,
this path of the master's doctrine has been purified —
may people, casting aside jealousy, proceed on it.
Thus is completed this <s>Avayavinirākaraṇa</s> (Refutation of the Composite).
